summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and EmberGrid Cloud to explore a cloud-GPU partner integration. EmberGrid is interested in offering Redwood Dedicated/Private as a managed inference option on their platform; key topics covered were networking/VPC patterns, supported GPU hardware, benchmarking and sizing, security controls (KMS, SOC2), and commercial models. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Lena Rao (EmberGrid), Tomás Álvarez (EmberGrid), Priya Nair (EmberGrid)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, and with me is Daniel Cho our systems sales engineer. How's it going over there?
[00:18] Lena (EmberGrid): Hi Sofia, thanks for doing this, yeah excited — bit of a noisy morning here, but good.
[00:24] Tomás: Afternoon all.
[00:26] Daniel (Redwood SE): Hey, hi, nice to meet you all. We'll keep this fairly informal, want to learn about EmberGrid's partner goals and see where Redwood can fit as a managed inference option on your cloud.
[00:40] Priya (EmberGrid): Cool, high level — EmberGrid runs regionally distributed GPU pools, we do a mix of preemptible and reserved capacity. We're exploring tighter integrations with inference vendors to offer turnkey model endpoints to our customers.
[01:05] Sofia: Great, can you give us a quick outline of the typical customer use cases you see and the constraints — latency targets, data residency etc?
[01:22] Tomás: Mostly enterprise SaaS customers who need low-latency chat and embeddings. Target p95 latency 200-500ms for small models, 800ms+ for larger seq lengths, but they're flexible. Data residency is important — many customers want EU region placement and sometimes air-gapped or VPC-only deployments.
[01:45] Lena: Also revenue ops folks asked if we can offer a managed llm product without them doing infra. So we want something where we can plug in Redwood as a managed runtime and still own billing and some packaging.
[02:10] Daniel: That's helpful. On Redwood's side we have Hosted, Dedicated and Private. For partner scenarios like yours we often recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private depending on whether you want us to run the control plane or you want a customer-managed control plane.
[02:33] Priya: Quick question on control plane — what networking options do you support? We typically require VPC peering, private link, and strict egress controls.
[02:43] Daniel: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink patterns, and for Private deployments we can operate entirely in your customer VPC with no egress to public internet — we can integrate KMS/HSM for keys. There may be some initial tunnel setup for telemetry/backups depending on the config.
[03:05] Tomás: And how do you handle model variants and fallbacks? Some of our customers want cheaper lower-latency fallbacks when the big models are overloaded.
[03:15] Sofia: We have smart routing — you can define policies to route by latency, cost, or region. Automatic fallback to compatible model variants is supported so you can keep SLAs while optimizing cost.
[03:30] Lena: Nice. On the hardware side, what GPU types do you support and do you have quantized profiles?
[03:40] Daniel: We tested on A100, H100, and some partners run Ampere-based and some AMD instances — for partner deployments we typically publish recommended quantization profiles. We do continuous batching and kernel selection that adapts to seq length and batch distribution.
[04:02] Priya: Do you have any hard constraints on instance types? We run a mix including newer generation H-series and some older A100s.
[04:10] Daniel: Not hard constraints, but performance characteristics differ; our runtime will optimize, but for cost predictability we recommend pinned variants. We can help with a sizing exercise.
[04:26] Tomás: Pricing/commercial model question — if we resell Redwood-backed endpoints through EmberGrid, do you have partner revenue share or reseller program?
[04:36] Sofia: Yes, we have partner programs — reseller and OEM-like arrangements. Commercial details vary by commitment and whether Redwood control plane is used. We can share a partner one-pager and example pricing bands; we'll need to align on support SLAs and billing flow.
[04:56] Lena: Can you also support audit logs and compliance docs? One of our customers needs SOC2 plus encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[05:06] Daniel: We provide audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS or HSM. SOC2 is commonly requested; we have a compliance pack we can share.
[05:22] Priya: Great. Could you summarize the network topologies you support — for example if we want to host the runtime in our region but keep control plane with Redwood, is that possible?
[05:33] Daniel: Yes — that's what Dedicated often looks like. You can have dedicated GPU pools in your VPC with a reserved capacity contract; the control plane can be hosted by Redwood with private connectivity, or we can do Private where the control plane also sits in your environment. There are trade-offs in telemetry and auto-scaling.
[05:52] Tomás: Ok, that makes sense. On benching — how do you recommend we run perf tests? We want to compare across our H100, A100, and cheaper options with quantization.
[06:05] Sofia: We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet and a recommended test harness. Typically we run per-token latency tests, throughput curves, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimates. Daniel can help design a suite for your workloads and we'll include guidance on sequence lengths and batching.
[06:24] Daniel: For the test harness we recommend synthetic traffic and a small subset of real prompts. Cache warmup matters a lot — prefix caching and KV cache behaviors can skew initial results if not warmed.
[06:40] Lena: Noted — on security again, we also need to confirm data retention policies when processes run on our infra. Can we set retention windows and ensure logs are kept only locally?
[06:52] Daniel: Yes, retention windows and log export can be configured. For Private deployments logs can remain in your cloud storage; for Dedicate there's configurable retention we can control via policies.
[07:08] Tomás: Any customers doing similar partner integrations you can point to?
[07:12] Sofia: We have a couple of cloud partners and a few SI resellers doing similar setups, happy to share reference patterns — I'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[07:24] Priya: From the infra side, what network ports and outbound requirements should we plan for?
[07:30] Daniel: Minimal: control plane to agent heartbeats and telemetry on HTTPS egress; for Private we can use a private link and avoid public egress. We'll send a short network diagram and a list of endpoints/ports.
[07:44] Lena: Perfect, that'll help our security team.
[07:50] Sofia: Let's talk timelines — what kind of timeline would you envision for a pilot?
[07:55] Tomás: If we can get the initial technical details and a sizing, we could run a pilot in 3-6 weeks; faster if we prioritize.
[08:03] Sofia: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the checklist and docs out in a couple of days.
[08:08] Priya: Ok.
[08:10] [10:15] (discussion continues -- mid-meeting deep-dive)
[10:15] Daniel: Quick deep-dive — on batching: our runtime supports dynamic continuous batching, but we also let you control max batch size and latency targets. For bursty workloads we recommend a small padding and dynamic scaling policy so you don't pay for reserved but still meet p95 targets.
[10:40] Tomás: How does tokenization differences across models affect your routing? If a customer switches models mid-request, is there a cost implication?
[10:50] Daniel: Tokenization affects token counts but routing is model-aware; switching mid-request isn't typical, we prefer model variants used per request. Cost estimates come from our token accounting and are model-specific.
[11:05] Lena: Any gotchas with KV cache when using quantized models?
[11:12] Daniel: Sometimes caching interacts with decoder-only optimization; with aggressive quantization you might see slight quality drift, so we recommend eval sets to validate regressions. Our Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles per workload.
[11:28] Tomás: Speaking of quality — do you offer evals or regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
[11:34] Sofia: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals; we can integrate those into partner dashboards.
[11:44] Priya: Great. We also need to think about onboarding — what are the steps for integrating Redwood into our console/marketplace?
[11:53] Sofia: Typical flow: 1) sign an MOU, 2) run a sizing/bench, 3) pilot with a small set of customers, 4) create a packaged product in your marketplace with billing flow (resell or direct), and 5) go GA. We can provide a partner onboarding playbook.
[12:10] Tomás: For billing, can we meter usage and invoice from EmberGrid side?
[12:15] Sofia: Yes, reseller flows are supported; we'll need to agree on reporting and reconciliation cadence.
[12:22] [20:00] (some cross talk and clarifications)
[20:05] Lena: One operational question — autoscaling and burst capacity. Our customers sometimes spike; will Redwood Dedicated allow bursts beyond reserved capacity?
[20:18] Daniel: Yes, we offer configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options; there's also fallback routing to hosted variants if capacity is exhausted.
[20:28] Priya: Does that mean potential data crossing boundaries? Like fallback to hosted might send data outside our VPC — is that a deal breaker?
[20:36] Sofia: That depends — if you need strict egress control, we can keep fallbacks within partner-managed resources by provisioning extra buffer capacity; otherwise there's an option to route to a hosted fallback with contractual constraints.
[20:52] Tomás: Good point, we'll need to map customer requirements.
[21:00] [30:00] (closing discussion)
[30:02] Sofia: To recap: Redwood will send partner one-pager, integration checklist, benchmark spreadsheet, network diagram, and compliance pack. EmberGrid will share GPU inventory and baseline perf metrics. Redwood to schedule technical deep-dive focused on VPC/EKS networking and benchmark plan.
[30:25] Lena: Sounds good.
[30:30] Tomás: We'll try to get metrics together by next week.
[30:35] Priya: Yep.
[30:38] Sofia: Any final questions?
[30:40] Priya: Not right now.
[30:42] Sofia: Great, thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[30:48] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings, some speaker overlap, proper nouns may be slightly off (EmberGrid spelled correctly but internal product names sometimes auto-corrected).
